 JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 28.11.2018 passed by III Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Dharwad in MVC.no.162/2016, this appeal is filed.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts as stated are that as result of grievous injuries sustained in accident occurred on 21.02.2015 due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle bearing registration no.KA-15-TZ- 008433/2014-15 by its rider, Smt.Saroja Palekar traveling pillion died.

3. Alleg ing loss of dependency due to her untimely death, her children filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'M.V. Act' for short) against owner and insurer of offending motorcycle.
4. On service of summons, owner did not contest.
He was placed ex-parte.

Only insurer filed objections alleg ing that rider of motorcycle did not have driving licence and therefore, there was The Divisional Manager vs Aditya S/O Satish Palekar on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/66821003/
2 violation of policy condition by insured .

sentences.text: 5. Thereafter, trib unal framed issues, recorded evidence of claimant no.1 as PW-1 and marked Exhibits P1 to P7.
In rebuttal, official of insurer was examined as RW1 and Exhib its R1 and R2 were marked.

6. On consideration, trib unal held that accident had occurred due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle by its rider, insurance policy issued was valid on date of accident and insurer was liable to pay compensation.

It held claimants were entitled for compensation as follows:
Amount in Sl.no. Heads Rupees 1. Loss of dependency 6,72,000/-
2. Loss of love and affection 1,00,000/-
Loss of estate, funeral expenses 3. 30,000/-
and obsequies.
Aggrieved by said award, insurer is in appeal.
8. Smt. Sharmila M. Patil, learned advocate appearing for insurer - appellant submitted that insured vehicle was under temporary registration.
As it was not permanently registered, owner was prosecuted for offences under Section 39 read with Section 192 of M.V. Act.
Therefore, contended that fastening of liability upon insurer was unsustainable.
9. On other hand , Sri. Harish S. Maigur, learned counsel for claimants supported impugned award and sought dismissal of appeal.
It was submitted that contention regarding registration of offending motorcycle having lapsed was not urged by insurer in its objections filed before trib unal.
No specific issue was framed.
Main contention urged before tribunal was about lack of driving licence by rider.
But as per Ex.P7 - ex tract of driv ing licence, licence to ride motorcycle with gear was issued on 17.12.2012 and valid as on date of accident.

It was submitted that without raising objections,
contention regarding lapse of registration could not be raised for first time in appeal.

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and certified copies of objections, deposition and exhibits made availab le for perusal of this Court by learned counsel for claimants.

11. From above submission, only point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether tribunal was justified in hold ing insurer liable to pay compensation?"
12.
Bare perusal of objections filed as well as deposition of RW-1 would reveal that specific contention regarding lapse of temporary registration is not taken in objections.
Though, in affidav it - examination-in-chief, copy of temporary registration certificate is stated to be produced, same is not marked.
Careful perusal of deposition would ind icate that contention urged was that insured vehicle was not permanently reg istered as on date of accident.
But, same was not substantiated with either documentary evidence or by examining RTO.

In absence of such effort before trib unal,
contention urged in first ap peal cannot be considered.

Even submission that an order of pay and recov er be passed, merely on ground that owner was prosecuted for offence under Section 39 of M.V. Act, would not be of any help to insurer when there is no material to estab lish that conviction followed charge.
13. Consequently, point for consideration is answered in negative.

14. In result, I pass following:
O R D E R i. Appeal is d ismissed.
ii. Insurer is d irected to deposit compensation within six weeks.

Sd/-
